open_questions.question: Does a full self-consistent BdG exact diagonalization on the CuO2 lattice (paper Appendix B) reproduce the split Q/2 peak in the LDoS at E=30 meV, not just in the assumed analytic order-parameter field?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Our replication assumes the cos(theta-theta_a) form of the induced CDW. The paper claims (Figs 6,7) that ED confirms this profile. Verifying it from ED closes the loop between phenomenology and microscopics.
open_questions.next_step: Implement the d-wave + PDW BdG mean-field Hamiltonian on a ~40x40 lattice with a single vortex, diagonalize, compute LDoS(r,E=30meV), and FFT the Q/2 component.

open_questions.question: Does the peak splitting delta_q converge to the predicted 1/xi as grid resolution and box size increase?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Our coarse grid gives delta_q ~ 0.157 vs predicted 1/xi ~ 0.067. Confirming convergence validates the quantitative prediction, not just the qualitative double-peak.
open_questions.next_step: Run a convergence sweep over N (256->1024) and L (160->640a); fit delta_q vs 1/xi across several xi values.

open_questions.question: How robust is the split-peak discriminator to disorder-averaged, incoherent vortex halos (real STM data averages many vortices)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The paper notes signals from different halos are incoherent unless each vortex is recentered. Real experiments have pinning disorder that may smear the split.
open_questions.next_step: Superpose many vortices at random positions with/without recentering, add noise, and test whether the split survives ensemble FFT.

open_questions.question: Can the canted-PDW vs uni-directional-PDW variants be distinguished by the direction/anisotropy of the split (theta_a dependence)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The paper proposes the split direction encodes theta_a and could separate PDW sub-scenarios; this is a sharper experimental prediction than PDW-vs-CDW alone.
open_questions.next_step: Sweep theta_a and the relative x/y PDW amplitudes; map the 2D FFT split direction and C4-breaking anisotropy.

open_questions.question: Does the harmonic period-4 (Q) CDW (CDWA/CDWB, Eqs 10-11) show a correlated but distinct FFT signature that co-varies with the period-8 split?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The paper predicts the period-8 and its period-4 harmonic share the same winding-induced blurring; a joint signature would be a stronger combined test.
open_questions.next_step: Construct the Q-CDW fields from the same PDW amplitudes, FFT, and correlate the period-4 peak structure with the period-8 split.
